note: Declared route capability table. Every exported HTTP handler under web/app/api appears here, at method grain. status 'declared' requires a catalog capability key; status 'none' asserts the handler legitimately requires none and must state why; status 'pending' is W-15's burndown backlog and is ratcheted downward only. Enforced by scripts/checkRouteCapabilities.mjs (prebuild) and locked by tests/access/routeCapabilityDeclaration.test.ts (RL-10). W-14 delivers the mechanism and the pilot slice; W-15 drives pending to zero.

ratchet.$comment: Lowered 694 -> 693 by OD-8's conversion of admin/users GET. The ratchet is TIGHT by test: the suite fails if the ceiling can be lowered further without producing a violation, so every conversion must bring it down and no conversion can be banked as slack.

inherited.$comment: Handlers that entered web/app/api from OTHER programs while this branch was frozen, and are therefore not part of the Access backlog `ratchet.max_pending` bounds. The effective assertion is `pending - inherited <= max_pending`, so the program-owned backlog stays ratcheted at its committed ceiling and the ceiling is NOT raised. Every entry must still exist, still be exported, and still be `pending`: a deleted route, a removed method, or a handler that has since been classified `declared` or `none` FAILS until it is removed from this list. The list may only shrink. Nothing here asserts anything about a handler's authorization - these are W-15 backlog items awaiting OD-7 exactly like every other `pending` entry, and none of them is exempt from it. Shape follows the sibling gate scripts/checkServiceClientPrincipal.mjs, whose `baseline` list is the same idea for the same backlog. 2026-08-19, OD-2 reconciliation: merging current origin/staging brought five handlers this table had never seen. Three are participant token routes and took the settled `none` classification of their fourteen siblings rather than being seeded pending. The two on app/api/admin/communications/ingress-routes are Communications' and are enumerated here — gated by requireAdminOrgContextLight, an admission helper, consulting no catalog capability, exactly like the seventeen before them. The ceiling was NOT raised to absorb them. 2026-08-20, post-merge staging repair: the Communications lane merged app/api/communications/unsubscribe between this census's last run and the PR #475 merge, so staging's build failed on an undeclared route. Enumerated here rather than classified `none`: it is gated by an HMAC-signed recipient token, which is plausibly the same 'the credential is in the request' doctrine as the public-form family, but no sibling carries a settled review for signed unsubscribe tokens and this census does not assert another program's authorization model on inference. The ceiling was NOT raised.
inherited.frozen_by: Access & Identity V2 recovery onto current staging. The recovered W-14 table was authored against the route tree at merge-base 08e9dd878; 459 staging commits later 20 handlers exist that it had never seen. Audited one by one: NONE consults a catalog capability, so none can be `declared`; 10 are gated by requireAdminOrOps (membership + portal eligibility, not authorization), 7 are authenticated-only org context, 3 are public token routes whose closest siblings are themselves pending. Classifying any of them is the OD-7 conversion decision, which a recovery does not make.

w15_classification.$comment: W-15's classification under OD-7, kept beside the table it describes so it cannot drift from it. tests/access/routeCapabilityDeclaration.test.ts asserts these counts against the LIVE gate inventory, so a stale figure here is a failing test rather than a stale document.
w15_classification.policy: OD-7: a non-capability gate converts to the canonical capability representing the operation it protects, and the conversion MUST NOT widen admission.

access_owned.state: EXHAUSTED. Every Access-owned handler is declared, reviewed `none`, or a recorded exception. OD-8 resolved the admin/users GET exception with deployed Q15 evidence, leaving ONE — send-password-reset POST, which is decision-gated for a reason other than OD-7.

conversion_exceptions.reason: Decision-gated for a reason OTHER than OD-7. This is W-38's subject — the credential-mail primitive bounded by the caller's org — which the plan gates on AD-15. OD-7 does not release it.

w15_classification.systemic_finding_blocking_the_remaining_: The 292 gate-helper handlers are NOT mechanically convertible under OD-7 alone, and the reason is structural rather than per-route. `requireAdminOrOps` resolves through getAdminOrgContextLight, which refuses unless `portalEligible` — it admits by ROLE, not by grant. So a pure capability swap admits capability holders who are not portal-eligible, which WIDENS (rule 6), while `portal AND capability` NARROWS for any portal principal whose org lacks the grant. Choosing between them, and proving which applies, needs per-org grant coverage from a real tenant — the same class of evidence the Q15 gate names, which the seeded certification tenant cannot supply because it defines only admin and ops.
w15_classification.remaining_by_ownership: 694 owned pending handlers across 142 route families — forms, communications, commercial, analytics, departments, processing, financials, jobs, opportunities, schedules, workflows and others. Every one carries another program's domain semantics, so the canonical capability for each is that domain's call, not Access's. OD-7 scopes this burndown to Access-owned sites and those are exhausted.

GET.note: Recorded, not imposed. This handler already calls the very assertDocumentAccess that documents/[id]/signed-url and vendors/[id]/documents/signed-url both declare as documents.read, and already refuses on decision.outcome !== 'allowed' before the URL is minted. The table was under-reporting: it sat 'pending' while enforcing. Declaring it changes who may call this route by nothing at all, which is what makes it Director-ownable where the rest of W-15 is not. The check runs inside `if (doc)` because that is the only branch that discloses anything — the no-document fall-through returns metadata the person read already carries. POST and DELETE stay pending deliberately: they gate on ctx.role !== 'admin', which is a gate but not a capability gate, and which key replaces a raw role check is W-15's product call.

OD-7 read/write rule: a READ surface converts to its canonical `.read` capability. The gate is `requirePortalOrUsersRolesManageAuth`, which accepts `settings.users_roles.read` as well as the manage key — so declaring the manage key here UNDER-DESCRIBED the gate. No code changed and no admission moved; the declaration now names what the handler actually enforces.

OD-8 closed this W-15 exception. It was `pending` not for want of a decision but because it failed OD-7's no-widening test: settings.users_roles.read resolves WITHOUT portalEligible, so a custom-role holder would have gained the roster read, and rule 6 forbids closing that with a secondary role check. Q15 answered both halves on the deployed tenant — C1 = 0 (no role outside admin/ops holds the key, so the widening population is empty) and B4 (ops lacked it in 2 orgs, so converting first would have NARROWED). Sequence: 20260819140000 grants ops the read key and fails closed on coverage, then the gate converted. The DISCLOSURE half is unchanged — addresses are still projected against canManageUsersAndRoles, and OD-8 does not authorize settings.users_roles.
